I have been working this land for sixty years. My father farmed before me, and I learned by watching and doing. I do not need papers to tell me how to farm — the soil here, the rains, the cold winters, I know all of it in my bones.

My 16.9 mu has grown wheat and maize in rotation my whole life. It is what this land is suited for, and I will not change that. The wheat goes in around Hanlu (Cold Dew, early October), and after I harvest it in June, I put maize in right away without wasting time.

**Wheat:** I will use the Jimai variety — I have grown it for over fifteen years and it does well on my soil. I apply base fertilizer before planting: mainly urea and diammonium phosphate mixed with some potash. I irrigate four times — before freezing, at jointing, heading, and grain filling. My well never fails me. I spray herbicide early, then check for rust and aphids near heading stage. Rotary till before sowing as I always do.

**Maize:** I buy hybrid seed from the village supply store — Zhengdan 958 or similar, whatever they have that I know. After wheat I seed directly without plowing — saves my back and my time at my age. I apply fertilizer at planting and top-dress at the knee-high stage. I irrigate at establishment if it is dry and again at tasseling. I spray for weeds right after emergence and once more for corn borer if I see them.

Three people in my household — my wife and I are old now. We hire a neighbor's machine for harvesting. I keep costs steady and do not gamble on new methods.
